skill.author: ACSKamloops

security_audit.summary: Most static backtick findings are false positives because SKILL.md is Markdown and many snippets are inline file names or read-only references. Several findings remain confirmed because the skill directs agents to execute repository-local Python and workflow scripts. The file also contains prompt-injection style role and workflow override language.

remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before tests, health checks, cleanup, approval, or reconciliation commands run. Document expected side effects for each command.
Reword role instructions as scoped guidance. State that system, developer, and active user instructions always take precedence.
Separate read-only checks from mutating actions. Require a dry run and user approval before cleanup or manager approval changes files.

content.value_statement: Complex evidence workflows can lose context, citations, and handoff discipline. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a structured manager role for planning, delegation, tests, and audits.
actual_capabilities: Defines a manager-planner role for Pukaist agent coordination.
Requires a step-by-step plan before delegated work begins.
Names the Gatekeeper, Analyst, Scribe, Archivist, Historian, and Barrister roles.
Specifies integrity tests, health checks, and cleanup review steps.
Defines audit checks for logs, queues, citations, and refined outputs.
Lists criteria for a healthy evidence workflow.
limitations: Assumes the Pukaist repository layout and named workflow files exist.
Depends on external scripts that are not included in this skill file.
May require shell access to inspect files and run repository checks.
Guides agent behavior but does not perform work by itself.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Evidence Intake
use_cases.description: Create a plan that assigns intake, OCR, review, and consolidation tasks to the right Pukaist roles.

use_cases.title: Audit Citation Quality
use_cases.description: Check whether evidence outputs use neutral language, valid citations, and traceable source references.

use_cases.title: Review Repository Health
use_cases.description: Guide health checks for queues, logs, orphan files, and stalled tasks before major workflow changes.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Simple Task
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the manager-planner skill to plan my next evidence workflow task. Keep the plan short and wait for approval before action.

prompt_templates.title: Check System Health
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the manager-planner skill to review system health. Identify which tests, logs, queues, and outputs need checking before work continues.

prompt_templates.title: Delegate a Multi-Step Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the manager-planner skill to break this request into Gatekeeper, Scribe, Analyst, and Archivist responsibilities. Include acceptance criteria for each handoff.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Completed Batch
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the manager-planner skill to audit a completed evidence batch. Check citation quality, neutral wording, queue status, and communication log closure.

output_examples.input: Plan intake for a new set of evidence files.
output_examples.output: The response provides a short role-based plan, asks for approval, and names the expected handoff outputs.

output_examples.input: Check whether the evidence workflow is healthy.
output_examples.output: The response lists test status, queue risks, log checks, citation checks, and any blocked work that needs attention.

output_examples.input: Audit refined reports before final delivery.
output_examples.output: The response summarizes sampled files, citation validity, neutral language issues, and follow-up tasks for responsible roles.

best_practices: Use it only in repositories that follow the expected Pukaist file layout.
Confirm with the user before any script or cleanup command runs.
Review each generated plan against the active user request before delegation.
anti_patterns: Using it in unrelated projects without the named files, queues, and roles.
Allowing cleanup or approval commands to run without explicit review.
Treating generated evidence audits as legal advice or final legal analysis.

faq.question: What does this skill help coordinate?
faq.answer: It coordinates Pukaist agent planning, delegation, repository checks, evidence review, and workflow audits.

faq.question: Does it run tests by itself?
faq.answer: No. It instructs the assistant when tests or checks may be needed, but tool execution still needs user control.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: Is it useful outside a Pukaist repository?
faq.answer: Only partly. Many instructions depend on specific Pukaist paths, logs, queues, and role names.

faq.question: Can it replace human review?
faq.answer: No. It structures review work, but users should verify evidence, commands, and final decisions.

faq.question: What security caution applies?
faq.answer: The skill includes command instructions and strong role language. Review commands before execution and keep higher-priority instructions in control.
